lead.hed: Defense News: Denmark says a Greenland security deal puts NATO on Arctic watch
lead.insight: Defense News, Monday via Reuters: Denmark, Greenland, and the United States are set to sign a Greenland security agreement Tuesday at the U.N. General Assembly. Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen told TV2 the Arctic would not be left solely to Copenhagen or Washington, and that NATO would largely look after the region. The text is not public. President Trump said Friday the deal grants the United States permanent control; Denmark has not answered that claim.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Space Force photo by Heather Johnson · DVIDS 9707383 · Public domain · Thule Tracking Station (callsign POGO), 22nd Space Operations Squadron Detachment 7, Pituffik Space Base, Greenland, April 8, 2026.

political.hed: USNI: Abraham Lincoln pulls into Guam at 302 days on deployment
political.insight: USNI News, Saturday: USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72), Carrier Air Wing 9, and the destroyer USS Frank Petersen (DDG-121) pulled into Guam for a logistics stop, U.S. 7th Fleet said. The carrier left the South China Sea this week via the Sulu Sea, according to ship spotters cited by USNI. Port call on the way home, not the San Diego return.

political.hed: USNI: Hormuz transits hit a three-week high as VLCC rates jump
political.insight: USNI News, Friday: non-Iranian-linked transits through the Strait of Hormuz climbed to 97 last week in preliminary Lloyd’s List Intelligence data, a three-week high, with very large crude carrier rates moving sharply. Preliminary counts, still subject to dark-transit adjustments.

political.hed: USNI: China Coast Guard rams a Philippine fisheries vessel
political.insight: USNI News, Friday: Chinese and Philippine maritime forces were in a ramming incident off Manila’s western island province, the latest high-profile South China Sea skirmish over maritime boundaries. Incident report with video, not a new treaty claim.

tech.hed: Defense News: French Army hunts “frugal” AI to hide on a see-through battlefield
tech.insight: Defense News, Friday from Besançon: Gen. Bruno Baratz, head of France’s Future Combat Command, said drone observation has created a “zone of death” on the front and a tactical stalemate. His command is looking at decoys, electronic warfare, and what he called frugal artificial intelligence that uses as little energy as possible. Command remarks, not a fielded system.

tech.hed: Defense News: Air Force leaders put a $14 billion hole in aircraft parts
tech.insight: Defense News, Friday from the Air, Space & Cyber Conference: Air Force Materiel Command’s Lt. Gen. Linda Hurry said the service has a $14 billion hole in supply, with aircraft down for parts up 87 percent over seven years. Panel figure, not an audited inventory.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Do not grade Congress on how fast it ships a preset bill
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Monday: Gallup has Americans about 80 percent dissatisfied with the country this year, and only 10 percent approved of Congress in April, with 86 percent disapproving. The essay argues the legislature should not be judged by how efficiently it produces predetermined outcomes. Essay, not a floor vote.

culture.hed: WORLD: Forced conversions and marriages still hunt Christians in Pakistan
culture.insight: WORLD, Thursday: 19-year-old Adan Sabir of Jaranwala says she was taken at gunpoint on July 3, 2025; her family filed a police report, and the accused produced forged marriage papers claiming conversion. She now moves in a burqa to hide. Field report on abduction and forced marriage, not a new statute.
